Understanding a kundli matching consultation

Kundli matching is a traditional astrological way of comparing two birth charts. A consultation gives you an opportunity to ask what a matching result means, what information it relies on and which parts need further explanation. It should be a conversation about the interpretation, rather than simply receiving a number.

What information is needed for both people?

Prepare each person's date of birth, birth time and birthplace. Check the spelling of the locations and whether a recorded time is morning or evening. Tell the astrologer about uncertain or missing details so they can explain the limits of the comparison. Share another person's details with their permission.

What does the Guna Milan score mean?

In the traditional Ashtakoot approach, eight areas of comparison contribute to a total out of 36. Ask the astrologer to explain the individual areas as well as the overall result. A score is part of that tradition's interpretation; it is not a measurement of how successful a relationship will be.

Is a score enough to decide about marriage?

No single score can settle a personal decision about marriage. Discuss communication, values, consent, responsibilities and practical expectations with your partner. If you seek an astrological reading, ask how the astrologer considers the wider charts and any uncertainty in the birth information.

What if the birth time is unknown?

Say so at the beginning. Ask which observations depend on an accurate time and which parts cannot be assessed confidently. Avoid selecting a convenient time just to obtain a result.

Can I ask about Mangal or Nadi concerns?

You can bring these questions to an astrologer who offers marriage or kundli consultations. Ask for a clear explanation of the method, context and limitations. You should not feel pressured into making a relationship decision or buying a remedy because of a frightening prediction.
